description: Snowflake stores OBJECT / VARIANT values in a canonical form: object keys are sorted alphabetically because objects are unordered, and a whole-valued decimal drops its scale so 406.0 becomes 406. Frostlake keeps OBJECT and ARRAY values as JSON text and compares them by that text, so two objects differing only in key order or number scale must serialise identically - otherwise EXCEPT, DISTINCT and = would wrongly treat them as distinct, which the two EXCEPT tests here pin. Canonicalisation is recursive through nested objects, arrays keep their order while each object element is still key-sorted, a NUMBER(38,0) beyond double precision embeds exactly (doubleValue() used to turn 21000000006420544706 into 21000000006420546000 inside VARIANT payloads), and OBJECT_INSERT / OBJECT_DELETE keep the canonical order. Converted 1:1 from functions/ObjectCanonicalizationTest (now retired). One assertion is expressed differently: the Java read PARSE_JSON('null') through String.valueOf and compared it to the text "null", which a SQL NULL would also satisfy - the converted test pins the real claim, that it is a JSON null (IS_NULL_VALUE true) while PARSE_JSON(NULL) is a SQL NULL.

steps.sql: SELECT OBJECT_CONSTRUCT('s', 406) EXCEPT SELECT OBJECT_CONSTRUCT('s', ROUND(405.958))
